newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firms with stronger NYMEX gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firms with stronger NYMEX gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures gained on Friday in sympathy with firmer U.S. markets pulled higher by stronger gasoline futures, traders said.
August Brent was 15 cents firmer at $18.11 a barrel at 1505 GMT after touching a high of $18.15.

Front month August gasoline was at 59.65 cents a gallon in New York, 0.25 cents off the high. Brokers said there had been talk that a trader was short of east coast product and buyers piled into the market to try and squeeze him out.
Further support came from a report that Venezuela shortly plans to announce a 25 percent rise in domestic gasoline prices.
The gasoline strength boosted NYMEX crude, which was at $19.38 a barrel after touching a high of $19.44.
Brokers saw resistance at $18.15/$18.18 on Brent and at $19.45 on crude.
Volume in London remained very thin as dealers awaited a meeting on Sunday between the U.N. Iraq coordinator and Iraqi officials for more talks on Baghdad's aid distribution plan.
Prices fell sharply on Thursday when the German government said it planned to sell oil from its reserves in order to qualify for Europe's single currency.
Bonn said on Friday it would sell 2.8 million barrels of oil in the next few weeks and dispose of its entire strategic reserves of 7.3 million tonnes of crude oil.
